title: Positional selectors written as An+B pick the wrong siblings at the boundaries
title_original: Fix :nth-child/:nth-of-type matching for An+B index boundaries
text_original:
`:nth-child(An+B)` / `:nth-of-type` (and their `-last-` variants) silently match the wrong elements — usually nothing — for several valid `An+B` micro-syntaxes, disagreeing with the CSS spec and lxml/every browser: ```pycon >>> import soupsieve as sv >>> from bs4 import BeautifulSoup >>> div = BeautifulSoup("
" + "" * 3 + "
", "html.parser").div >>> len(sv.select(":nth-child(2n-2)", div)) # should match the 2nd child 0 >>> len(sv.select(":nth-child(n-1)", div)) # should match all children 0 >>> div5 = BeautifulSoup("
" + "" * 5 + "
", "html.parser").div >>> len(sv.select(":nth-child(n+5)", div5)) # should match the 5th child 0 ``` Per the spec, `:nth-child(an+b)` matches an element whose 1-based index equals `a·n + b` for some integer `n ≥ 0`, so `n-1` (indices 1, 2, 3, …) should match every child and `n+5` should match the 5th. Existing tests pass only because their markup is large enough that these sequences never land exactly on index 0 and `b` stays within the child count. ### Cause `CSSMatch.match_nth` picks the starting `count` (`n`) with a hand-rolled loop that walks the index toward the valid range using signed "diff" heuristics. It has three boundary faults: it treats index `0` as "not too low" (so a step landing on `0` aborts down the wrong branch), it bounds the search to `<= last_index` while the evaluation loop accepts `<= last_index + 1` (so the case where the only match is the last child bails out early), and the `a < 0` branch stops early for some inputs. ### Fix Replace the heuristic with the direct closed form for the first in-range `n`: - `a > 0`: the smallest `n` with `a·n + b >= 1` — `0` when `b >= 1`, otherwise `ceil((1 - b) / a)`. - `a < 0`: the largest such `n`, then walk `n` downward so the index ascends as the evaluation loop (unchanged) walks the children. The result is a net reduction in code and matches the spec. ### Verification - Full test suite passes (394 passed). - New `test_nth_child_an_plus_b_boundaries` covers the child- and last-child boundary forms, with expected results cross-checked against lxml. - Differential fuzz vs `lxml`/`cssselect` over 12,000 random cases (`:nth-child` / `nth-of-type` / `nth-last-*`, `a, b` over `[-4..4] × [-6..6]`, 1–10 children, mixed tag types, with and without inter-tag whitespace): **0 disagreements** after the fix (738 before). - `ruff check .` and `mypy` are clean.
text_rewritten:
:nth-child() and :nth-of-type(), and their -last- variants, disagree with every browser and with the CSS specification for several perfectly valid An+B forms. When the arithmetic sequence steps onto index 0, when the only qualifying element is the last sibling, or when the step is negative, the selector picks the wrong elements -- usually nothing at all. A form whose sequence of 1-based indices covers every sibling should select every sibling; a form whose only in-range index is the last sibling should select that sibling.

Per the specification, an An+B form matches an element whose 1-based index among its siblings equals a*n + b for some integer n >= 0. The established forms -- odd, even, a bare integer, the common 2n+1 shape -- are fine today and must stay that way; it is the boundary cases that are wrong.
body:
:nth-child() and :nth-of-type(), and their -last- variants, disagree with every browser and with the CSS specification for several perfectly valid An+B forms. When the arithmetic sequence steps onto index 0, when the only qualifying element is the last sibling, or when the step is negative, the selector picks the wrong elements -- usually nothing at all. A form whose sequence of 1-based indices covers every sibling should select every sibling; a form whose only in-range index is the last sibling should select that sibling.

Per the specification, an An+B form matches an element whose 1-based index among its siblings equals a*n + b for some integer n >= 0. The established forms -- odd, even, a bare integer, the common 2n+1 shape -- are fine today and must stay that way; it is the boundary cases that are wrong.
acceptance_hint: For every An+B form the selector matches exactly the siblings whose 1-based index equals a*n + b for some n >= 0, including forms whose sequence crosses index 0 or lands only on the last sibling; established forms such as odd and 2n+1 are unchanged.
